title: Allergist visit
what: A doctor who finds out what you are allergic to and chooses treatment.
why: For seasonal runny nose and sneezing, rashes and itching, reactions to food, medicines, or stings, and asthma.
tell_doctor: What you reacted to, when, and what it looked like
What allergy medicines you take, and when you last took them
Any severe reactions with swelling or trouble breathing
If you have asthma or eczema

prepare.title: Allergy medicines
prepare.text: If skin tests are planned, some medicines affect the result. Do not stop them on your own. Ask the doctor in advance, and they will decide.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write down when reactions happen and after what. Photos of a rash help too.

bring: Allergy test results, if you had them
Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your reactions in detail
Your skin, nose, and throat are checked
The doctor decides if skin tests or a blood test are needed
You learn how to avoid the allergen and get treatment
feel: The exam itself is not unpleasant
If skin tests are done, light pricks and itching at the test spots
after: The doctor may give you an action plan for a severe reaction
Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own
red_flags: Swelling of the lips or tongue, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness after contact with an allergen: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have tests at the first visit?
faq.a: Sometimes, but often you need to prepare first. Check with the clinic.

faq.q: Should I stop allergy medicines before the visit?
faq.a: Do not stop them on your own. Tell the doctor what you take, and they will decide.

reminders.text: Allergist visit tomorrow. Write down the allergy medicines you take, and bring past test results.
